sermon.title: Standing
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer shows the Levites were set apart to stand before the Lord and minister to him, a calling offered to all Israel and renewed under Hezekiah, who saw God defeat Assyria, while Joash fell after forsaking it. Believers are now a royal priesthood offering spiritual sacrifices, and praise silences the enemy. He closes on the Holy Spirit, who sends, speaks, delivers, gifts and changes us.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Points to check: 2 Chronicles 29 spoken as “second Corinthians 29”; 2 Chronicles 32 spoken as “31”; Psalm 8:2 spoken as “Psalms 82”; 60% church attendance in the 1950s; “twice as many accounts of praise” as worship; dry lightning explanation. Sensitive content kept as spoken: Detroit police (“the big four”) beating corner youths; liberals and 52% of Democrats want socialism and won’t punish criminals; Catholic exorcism ritual “hokey pokey”; witch doctors in Ghana’s Volta region; Jewish services as debate; young “self-appointed ministers”.

John 4:24: worship in spirit and truth.

faqs.question: Why stand before the Lord?
faqs.answer: It gives him your attention, as the Levites did.

faqs.question: Does Exodus 19 attach conditions?
faqs.answer: Yes, obey my voice and keep my covenant.

faqs.question: Has God’s order changed over the ages?
faqs.answer: No, he is the same yesterday, today and forever.

faqs.question: Is worship a deeper life than praise?
faqs.answer: No, the same Spirit brings both.

faqs.question: What are spiritual sacrifices?
faqs.answer: Standing, lifting hands, singing, clapping, kneeling and dancing in praise.

faqs.question: Who is qualified to praise God?
faqs.answer: Anyone who has accepted Jesus’ death for them.

faqs.question: Can you claim all nine gifts?
